text:
sam: Heads-up —usz2 GPU pool failing node join after a KMS policy tweak during the region-peering test. Nodes hang on 'decrypt keystore' and never finish startup. anyone seeing this?

lia: saw a couple of alerts. which pool/az? logs? :eyes:

sam: cluster=ml-prod-usw2, pool=gpu-pool-3, az=usw2-b. logs look like repeated decryption errors: 
```
2026-03-23T10:12:01Z ERROR keystore: decrypt failed: AccessDenied: User "arn:aws:sts::999999999999:assumed-role/node-role/..." is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:888888888888:key/abcd-ef01
```

jordan: that ARN is the node's STS. Did the recent KMS grant change scope to account-only? We scoped grants to account:888888888888 yesterday. if peering or privatelink -> cross-account flows break.

mei: Confirmed — we changed the KMS key policy during the audit-hardening rollout to only allow principals from the primary account and the new audit shipper role. That would block decrypts from nodes that assume a cross-account role via peering.

sam: ah — the test peered an EU analytics VPC into USW2 for model evals. nodes that spawn under that peering path are getting a different assumed-role ARN (cross-account).

ops-bot: alert: 18 nodes in gpu-pool-3 stuck in Pending -> FailedJoin. Median join time 0m -> 12m. Incident created: INC-2026-1473

lia: quick question — can we grant the specific assumed-role ARNs instead of broadening the key policy? We should avoid rollback if possible.

jordan: yes but the roll-forward path is fiddly: need to enumerate role ARNs from the peered account/cluster and add kms:Decrypt grants. I can script a grant but it needs owner approvals.

mei: alternative temporary workaround: route keystore traffic over the privatelink proxy in primary account — nodes will hit proxy's principal and decrypt will succeed. That avoids changing the key policy immediately. Drawback: single proxy > hotspot and extra egress NAT costs.

sam: cost tradeoff noted. how bad is the hotspot risk? we have 3 proxy instances in us-west-2 behind ALB. adding 18 nodes is fine short term but if we scale 100s it's a problem.

jordan: scripting grants is quick: sample AWS CLI below. will test in staging, then run in prod with lia's OK.
```
aws kms create-grant --key-id alias/ml-keystore --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::999999999999:role/peered-node-role --operations Decrypt
```

lia: runbook: 1) mitigation = add grant for peered role (quick), 2) postmortem/perm fix = update onboarding to create scoped grant automatically for peered accounts or use privatelink-only keystore. which do we pick?

mei: recommend mitigation + scheduled change to onboarding. privatelink-only needs infra work and will take days.

sam: ok let's do mitigation now. jordan — test grant in staging, post results here. if green, lia please approve prod run. i'll open a short-term paging policy to watch proxy latencies and cost.

jordan: testing in staging now. log from staging node shows decrypt success after grant applied: 
```
2026-03-23T10:34:12Z INFO keystore: decrypt OK, kvcache restored
```

jordan: staging looks good. will prepare prod command and tag with runbook ID RB-2026-09.

lia: approved. please add the exact ARNs you grant to the incident ticket and include expiry TTL on the grant if possible. prefer 72h ttl while we finalize onboarding changes.

sam: noted — ops-bot created INC-2026-1473 and linked RB-2026-09. thumbs up to quick grant + follow-up. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: annotation: mitigation applied in prod at 2026-03-23T10:50:00Z by jordan. 18 nodes recovered, 0 nodes remaining pending. Monitoring: 1h.

mei: i'll schedule a follow-up retro tomorrow to decide either: automated cross-account grant on peer onboarding OR default to privatelink-keystore (longer but cleaner). put the cost estimate and latency tradeoffs on the retro doc.

sam: thanks all. closing loop once the retro has a decision. if anything regresses ping @oncall.
